maya: Quick dump from this morning's long-ctx sweep on Mistral-24B (NTK RoPE). saw oscillating perplexity at ~6k-12k token range, and latency spikes tied to kernel fallback.
sam: ugh. is this the same jitter we saw last month or a new pattern?
maya: similar symptoms but different trigger. profile attached (snippet below). spikes correlate with headkv eviction churn and a kernel switch from fast-atten to slow-atten at runtime.
jin: can you paste the profiler flame or the cmd you ran?
maya: sure. run: `./bin/ropexp --model mistral-24b-ntk --max_len 16k --batcher windowed --kernel_pref fast,compat` logs:
```
[2026-03-15T08:21:12Z] seq=8000 tokens: kernel=fast-atten OK
[2026-03-15T08:21:12Z] seq=8050 tokens: kernel=slow-atten fallback latency +23ms
[2026-03-15T08:21:12Z] KV evict: headkv_slots=0.78 -> 0.55
[2026-03-15T08:21:12Z] perplexity jump: 12.4 -> 18.9
```
zara: i reproduced on Mixtral-8B too but at slightly different seq lengths (4k-7k). Qwen didn't show the same perplexity bump, but latency hit there was noticeable.
sam: could be head/kv dim interaction with RoPE exponent scaling. are we using linear or yarn variant for NTK? maya: NTK-YARN hybrid. coefficient schedule: `alpha=0.9` early, drifting to `alpha=1.1` past 6k.
jin: that alpha drift could push phase into aliasing region for some heads -> head split saturation -> kv churn. we have seen similar in the headsplit paper.
maya: i tried forcing `ropexp_mode=linear` and the perplexity spike went away, but mean latency slightly higher overall.
sam: so tradeoff: linear stable quality, NTK better average latency but brittle at longctx.
perf-bot: [benchmark ci] mistral-24b-ntk longctx sweep: p99 latency +18ms vs baseline, perplexity delta +4.6 at 8k-10k. See /ci/bench/1777770001
devops: any chance this is cache eviction due to batching heuristic? windowed batcher might be increasing concurrent KV memory pressure.
zara: i ran same with `batcher=max_tokens` and memory pressure lower, no kernel fallback, but throughput dropped 8%.
sam: maybe add an adaptive backoff: prefer `slow-atten` earlier when headkv_slots < 0.6 instead of waiting for a kernel error.
jin: patch idea:
```
if headkv_util < 0.6 and seq_len > 4k:
    kernel_pref = ['slow-atten','fast-atten']
else:
    kernel_pref = ['fast-atten','slow-atten']
```
maya: that soft-pref switch removed the fallbacks in my local and smoothed perplexity, worth trying on canary.
sam: also need to log headkv_slots per request for a week to find model-specific safe ranges. maybe per-model config: mistral-24b safe headkv_min=0.65, mixtral-8b=0.5 etc.
perf-bot: added metric `headkv_slots` to perf dashboard and created alert when kernel_fallback_rate > 0.5%.
zara: one more odd thing: kv cache trace shows small KV slot fragmentation after certain tokens, not full eviction. might be our slot compaction heuristic.
jin: yep. compaction is O(n) and triggers under hybrid batching; causes short stall and forces kernel to re-evaluate path. fix is to do incremental compaction during idle or between micro-batches.
maya: i'll run a canary with: adaptive kernel pref + non-blocking compaction + batcher=max_tokens for 24h and report.
sam: note to self: add model config doc entry for `ropexp_safe_ranges` + `kernel_pref_policy` under /ops/ropexp/configs.
devops: heads-up: if canary passes, we'll need a small dedicated slot reservation for Mistral on prod to avoid noisy neighbors causing headkv < thresholds.
zara: thanks all. keeping this thread updated with canary logs. cc @perf-bot for perf deltas and @devops for capacity planning :thumbsup:
